title: Will the Truth Free Us from Misinformation?
eligible_reason: No staggered design. The empirical tests are (i) NFL beat-writer score predictions, a within-game double difference across writers regressed on a constant and week (Table 2, lm_robust(diffdiff ~ 1 + week + absline)), and (ii) a fact-check DiD (Table 4) comparing cable vs broadcast outlets before/after the single PunditFact launch week (post = week >= 2288 for all outlets) with a pooled cable dummy (CABdum), post, and a linear week trend (week_n), clustered by week. Single common treatment date, pooled treated-group dummy instead of outlet FE, and a linear time trend.
design_notes: Fact Check Replication Script.R lines 45-87: event <- 2288; post <- week >= event; CABdum = MSMCAB=='CAB'; lm_robust(pa_fa ~ post + CABdum + post*CABdum + week_n, clusters=week) within a 75-week window. Outlet-level variants (as.factor(outlet_d)*post + week FE) and FOX/CNN/MSNBC-only versions are Online Appendix (Tables WA.5-WA.6). Event-time bins pd1..pd10 (20-week bins) interact CABdum, still single date.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One event week (event <- 2288, PunditFact launch) common to all outlets.
data_files_note: Weekly PunditFact fact-check counts by outlet and NFL prediction data shipped as CSV/TXT.
screener_notes: Published PDF read (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2023.03896.pdf via data/text). Theory paper on strategic misinformation with two supporting empirical illustrations; neither is staggered.
